record.title: same_origin ignores the scheme, so a plaintext http:// page on the same host passes the CSRF origin check of a TLS deployment
record.description: Every cookie-authenticated UI mutation ultimately relies on same_origin() (api.py:108-110), which compares only urlsplit(Origin).netloc with the Host header and never the scheme. Verified in-sandbox: http://H, http://H:8765, and http://agentbox.example.com are all accepted against the matching Host, while sibling same-site, wrong port, and null are rejected. In a TLS deployment a page served as plaintext http://H (forgeable by an active network attacker; no Strict-Transport-Security is set anywhere in agentbox/ or deploy/, and Caddy's reverse_proxy adds none) has a different web origin from https://H but passes this check. On a browser WITHOUT schemeful same-site, http://H and https://H count as same-site, so a SameSite=Strict Secure cookie (desktop.py:53) is attached to the auto-submitted cross-scheme POST and agentbox accepts it. Id-free actions: POST /logout (ends the server session and hands desktop takeover back to the agent) and POST /ui/sandboxes (creates a sandbox with an attacker-supplied source_dir). Approve/deny additionally needs the 48-bit apr_ approval id. DECISIVE CAVEAT from parent-live evidence (agents/parent-live/artifacts/l3/l4.out): on current Chromium 141 the cross-scheme POST had same_origin accept its Origin but the Secure SameSite=Strict cookie was NOT attached (schemeful same-site is the modern default), so the session-ending and create attacks fail there; the only effect was the unconditional r.delete_cookie on the logout response clearing the browser cookie client-side (forced browser logout) WITHOUT ending the server session. The finding therefore stands only on legacy/non-schemeful browsers; the exploitable browser population and HSTS/active-network-attacker deployment remain the open facts.
record.claimed_root_cause: api.py:108-110: same_origin() accepts when urlsplit(origin).netloc == headers['host'] with no scheme comparison, so the cross-origin defence degrades to the browser treating http/https of one host as cross-site; nothing in source emits Strict-Transport-Security (deploy/Caddyfile and all of agentbox/ set none), so an active network attacker can serve http://H.

trace.scope: decide (POST /ui/approvals/{aid}/{decision}); also create web.py:160, logout web.py:128
trace.description: Cookie-authenticated, form-encodable POST routes reachable by a cross-origin auto-submitted form; verified these are the state-changing UI mutations gated only by the cookie session plus same_origin.
Resolves the cookie session via box.desktop.session_scope(cookie) (api.py:119), then same_origin(request.headers) at api.py:122 is the only origin binding for the cookie principal.
Returns True when urlsplit(origin).netloc equals Host; independently confirmed http://H matches Host H and missing Origin is allowed, so scheme is never compared.
box.decide(aid, approve, actor='human', session=p.session) executes with the victim's session; peer id-free sinks are create_sandbox at web.py:164 and end_ui_session at web.py:132.

evidence.description: Netloc-only comparison with no scheme check. Reproduced in-sandbox (agents/v01/artifacts/v01_same_origin.out): accepts http://H vs Host H, http://H:8765 vs H:8765, http://agentbox.example.com vs that host, and missing Origin; rejects sibling same-site, wrong port, and null.
set_cookie issues the session cookie HttpOnly, samesite='strict', secure=secure; under non-schemeful same-site http://H and https://H are same-site, so the Strict cookie is not separated by scheme.
s.secure_cookie = s.secure_cookie or tls or behind: the Secure attribute is set for direct-TLS and behind-TLS-proxy deployments, which is the deployment class this finding targets.
reverse_proxy site block emits no Strict-Transport-Security; grep over agentbox/ and deploy/ found no HSTS anywhere, so the browser is not forced to upgrade http://H to https.
logout's only guard is the scheme-blind same_origin (web.py:130); end_ui_session (web.py:132) ends the server session and hands takeover leases back to the agent when the cookie is present.

Parent-live real Chromium 141: cross-scheme POST http://127.0.0.1 -> https://127.0.0.1/logout had same_origin accept the http Origin (netloc==Host) but the Secure SameSite=Strict cookie was NOT attached (schemeful same-site); server session not ended, only the delete_cookie forced a client-side logout. Resolves the modern-browser case as non-exploitable and narrows the finding to legacy/non-schemeful browsers.

blockers: Browser behaviour (decisive): whether any operator browser lacks schemeful same-site and so attaches a SameSite=Strict Secure cookie to a cross-scheme form POST from http://H to https://H. Parent-live Chromium 141 did NOT attach it (schemeful same-site), so the meaningful attack fails on current Chromium/Firefox/WebKit defaults; the finding depends on legacy/non-schemeful browser versions, which source cannot determine.
Deployment: whether the production host sends HSTS or is preloaded (none in source), and whether an active on-path network attacker who can serve plaintext http://H is in scope.
Approve/deny requires the 48-bit apr_ approval id; a blind cross-origin attacker is limited to POST /logout and POST /ui/sandboxes.

validation_plan.local: Isolated loopback browser lab: map H to 127.0.0.1, run a dummy agentbox with --tls-cert (self-signed, lab-trusted) on 443 and a plaintext http://H listener on 80 auto-submitting forms to https://H/logout and /ui/sandboxes. The parent already ran this on Chromium 141 and the Secure SameSite=Strict cookie was not attached (agents/parent-live/artifacts/l3/l4.out). The remaining local step is a browser/version configured WITHOUT schemeful same-site (legacy Chrome <89 / Firefox <96 or the policy that disables it): log in to https://H, open http://H, and check whether agentbox_session is sent and the POST is accepted (200/303) rather than 403, and whether the server session is actually ended. Regression check on the fix: same_origin({'origin':'http://h','host':'h'}) must return False once the full scheme+netloc origin is compared.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner confirms whether the production hostname sends HSTS (or is on the preload list) and which browser versions operators actually use; if all are schemeful-same-site browsers and/or HSTS is present, the finding is not reachable. No live probing of deployed endpoints.
